record.paper_title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
record.original_question: Within branch-cut cosmology and its multiverse picture, how are the homogeneity of primordial radiation and the average density of matter established strongly enough to support the later formation of the structures observed in the universe today?

evidence.quote: And the ensuing questions, as the homogeneity of the primordial radiation and average density of matter as key elements for the formation of the structures observed today in the universe, among others.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cosmological model, called branch-cut cosmology, in which the conventional initial singularity of the standard Big Bang scenario is replaced by a Riemann-surface branch cut in the complexified scale factor. In this framework the early universe is described not by a single classical spacetime but by a multiverse-like collection of sheets joined along the branch cut, each carrying its own primordial radiation field and matter distribution. Assume the dynamics on each sheet is governed by a Friedmann-type evolution equation analytically continued through the branch cut, and that primordial radiation and matter are transported between sheets according to the multi-sheeted geometry.

Within this setting, give a quantitative mechanism that establishes:

(a) the spatial homogeneity of the primordial radiation field across each sheet of the branch-cut multiverse to a level consistent with the observed isotropy of the cosmic microwave background (relative temperature fluctuations of order 10^{-5}); and

(b) a sufficiently uniform average matter density, together with a power spectrum of small perturbations on top of it, such that gravitational instability during the subsequent evolution reproduces the large-scale structure (galaxies, clusters, filaments and voids) observed in the present universe.

Formulate explicitly the equations governing the propagation of perturbations across the branch cut, derive the resulting two-point correlation function of density fluctuations at the end of the primordial epoch, and show that the homogeneity and uniformity conditions in (a) and (b) follow from the geometric structure of the branch-cut multiverse rather than from an inflationary phase.
artifact.status_search_result: Branch-cut cosmology is a relatively recent proposal; the question of how homogeneity of primordial radiation and uniform average matter density are achieved—without invoking standard inflation—is explicitly listed as an open question in the program. No published derivation establishing these properties quantitatively within branch-cut cosmology appears to exist.

status_evidence.title: The Branch-Cut Cosmology: evidences and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Open questions including homogeneity of primordial radiation and average matter density as key elements for structure formation are discussed.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of explaining homogeneity and average matter density in branch-cut cosmology is stated as an open question.
